scenario.symptoms: After a cross-region network blip, two regions both accepted write traffic for 90 seconds. Order IDs collided and inventory counts diverged by 1,200 units.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Active-active deployment uses async replication with last-writer-wins. Failover detection relied on heartbeat timeouts without fencing tokens, so both regions believed they were primary.

incident.headline: Both regions accepted writes without fencing after partition healed

agenda.goal: Prevent dual-primary writes and reconcile safely after partitions.
agenda.opener: Inventory diverged after a short network split—how did split brain happen and how do you prevent it?

evidence.strong: Single writer via consensus or primary lease with fencing tokens, sticky routing during failover, and conflict repair playbook.
evidence.adequate: Mentions primary/secondary failover but not fencing or write quarantine during ambiguity.
evidence.weak: Active-active LWW on all rows without merge semantics.

misconceptions.pattern: Running two writable primaries for availability.
misconceptions.challenge: What happens to uniqueness constraints when both sides mint IDs?

probes: How do you fence the old primary when failover promotes EU?
Which workloads can be active-active vs single-writer?
hints: Leases need monotonic fencing tokens checked by storage.
agenda.referenceFix: Use a global primary with lease + fencing, route writes through a control plane that revokes old primaries, queue cross-region reads, and run deterministic merge jobs for the conflict window.

nuggets.title: Stale reads right after regional failover

scenario.symptoms: Failover to the secondary region succeeded in DNS, but users saw account balances from six hours ago for 20 minutes. Payment retries caused duplicate holds.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Read replicas in the DR region lagged behind the former primary. Traffic was shifted as soon as the health check on the app layer passed, before replication caught up.

incident.headline: Traffic routed to DR before replica caught up with last primary writes

agenda.goal: Fail over reads and writes only after data safety criteria are met.
agenda.opener: Users saw stale balances immediately after failover—what signal should have blocked traffic shift?

evidence.strong: Checks replication lag / LSN catch-up, promotes replica only after quorum, uses read-only mode until consistent, and idempotent payment APIs.
evidence.adequate: Mentions replication lag metric but no gating on DNS flip.
evidence.weak: Flips DNS when app health passes regardless of data lag.

misconceptions.pattern: Treating app health as sufficient for failover.
misconceptions.challenge: App can be up while database is hours stale—what do users read?

probes: What replication metric do you watch before serving writes in DR?
How do clients retry safely during ambiguity?
hints: Promotion and traffic shift are separate steps.
Idempotency keys prevent duplicate financial side effects.
agenda.referenceFix: Gate failover on replica lag below RPO, keep DR read-only until caught up or promoted cleanly, then shift DNS; enforce idempotent money APIs through the transition.

nuggets.title: DR region still calls failed primary

scenario.symptoms: Regional failover appeared successful, but checkout still failed because the DR stack synchronously called an identity service that remained pinned to the down region.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Hard-coded regional endpoints and a shared control plane in us-east-1 meant DR apps could not authenticate users after the primary region outage.

incident.headline: DR checkout depends on identity service in the failed region

agenda.goal: Make regional failover work end-to-end including dependencies.
agenda.opener: App failover succeeded but checkout still errors—what dependency did we miss?

evidence.strong: Regional service discovery, dependency maps, active/passive pairs per critical service, and failover drills that test auth/payments not just edge apps.
evidence.adequate: Lists dependencies but keeps single-region shared services without HA story.
evidence.weak: Assumes only the main app tier needs multi-region.

probes: Which dependencies must be multi-homed vs globally shared?
How does config propagate local endpoints during failover?
hints: Draw a dependency graph before designing failover.
Shared control planes are a common hidden single point of failure.
agenda.referenceFix: Run critical dependencies in each region with health-aware discovery, eliminate hard-coded region URLs, and automate config flip as part of the failover runbook.
